Actor.pilot: A player character: stats, skills, flight skills, Reserve and Rank/Fame.
Actor.aircraft: A warbird or enemy fighter with its own token. Uses the linked pilot's skills, or its crew block when flown by an NPC.
Actor.npc: A ground NPC: a thug (no Health track) or a full threat.
Actor.vessel: An airship, train, fortification or courier: a big target with Threat and sub-systems that fighters strafe.

Item.weapon: Aircraft guns, heavy ordinance, missiles, turrets or personal weapons.
Item.trait: A warbird trait whose modifiers feed the aircraft's ratings.
Item.maneuver: A stunt, defending option or BVR tactic, posted to chat when used.
Item.sponsorship: A sponsor or a contract worth Fame Points.
Item.gear: Personal equipment; armour adds to Resist while equipped.

standing.name: Standing stat
standing.hint: Jet Age and the historical sourcebooks replace Fame with military Rank. Pick which one pilot sheets show and use.

gritty.name: Gritty rules (Shoot to Kill)
gritty.hint: Jet Age optional rules: lives are always on the line in gunfights and in the air, and a pilot going down must roll 1d6 + Spirit vs 5 to bail out.

enemyGrades.name: Enemy pilot grades
enemyGrades.hint: Crew numbers used by the enemy flight generator; edited from the generator dialog.

Standing.scandalTooltip: While in a Scandal the Fame bonus becomes a penalty on Command, Etiquette, Perform, Persuade, Publicity and Interrogation rolls, item costs go up by 1 and items of value equal to Fame cannot be bought.
Standing.fameHint: Once per session Fame may be added to one roll of: {skills}. Fame is also wealth: items of lower value are bought freely, equal value needs a Barter roll vs 6 + value.
Standing.rankHint: Rank works like Fame: once per session add it to one roll of {skills} when dealing with the military, and it measures buying power. A higher Rank can always pull Rank on a lower one.
Standing.activeFP: Active sponsors are worth {fp} FP. More than 10 FP of sponsors makes the plane easy to spot (+1 to Awareness rolls against it).

WeaponFlag.extraDie: Extra die to hit (keep the best)
WeaponFlag.grouped: Grouped targets (one roll vs every target)
WeaponFlag.fragmentary: Fragmentary (no −2 vs people, hits everyone in the blast)

Formula.defence: Defence = 3 + Body + Athletics (+ shield, Life on the Line, wound penalty)
Formula.resist: Resist = Spirit + Armour from equipped gear
Formula.gunnery: 1d6 + SA + Gunnery + weapon Accuracy + traits (+ penalties)
Formula.ordinance: 1d6 + SA + Ordinance + weapon Accuracy + traits (+ Radar for missiles, + penalties)
Formula.ew: 1d6 + SA + Electronic Warfare + Radar + traits (+ penalties)
Formula.escapeDefence: Break Defence + 2 (+ traits). Super is added when disengaging.
Formula.stuntDefence: 1d6 + SA + Piloting + traits. Needs Performance 3+, not while Trailing Smoke or Crippled.

Pilot.standingTooltip: Rank or Fame, depending on the world setting.
Pilot.reserveTooltip: Reserve refreshes each session to highest skill + 2 (currently {suggested}). Spend +1 per point on a roll, up to +3.
Pilot.lifeOnTheLineTooltip: +1 to all rolls and Defence for the scene, but injuries become serious and death is possible.
Pilot.aircraftNotLinkedBack: This aircraft lists a different pilot. Open it and link this pilot to keep both sheets in sync.
Pilot.noAircraft: No aircraft assigned. Drag an Aircraft actor from the sidebar onto this sheet, or pick one.
Pilot.killPending: Kill for {name}: the pilot's owner or the GM can credit it
Pilot.milestoneLine: {name} is now a {milestone} ({air} air kills, {ground} ground kills). A new Warbird trait may be taken.

Aircraft.hardpointNotesPlaceholder: 4 Sparrows, 4 Sidewinders, 3 drop tanks or gun pods
Aircraft.fuelPlaceholder: Limited Fuel (1.75 hours, 2,600 km with drop tanks)
Aircraft.innateTraitsPlaceholder: Environmental Controls, Radio (100 km), Gun Camera, Refueling Probe
Aircraft.performanceHint: 0 building · 1 airship/train · 2 non-Guild fighter · 3 warbird · 4–5 elite · 6–7 top jets. Base value is editable below the dial; traits are added automatically.
Aircraft.armourHint: Armour = Resist for vehicles. Subtracted from damage (less the weapon's AP).
Aircraft.structureHint: Remaining / total Structure. The box below sets the base Structure; traits add to it.
Aircraft.drHint: Damage Resistance adds extra 0 boxes at the start of the Structure track.
Aircraft.radarHint: Radar Rating −3..+3 (F-4 = 0). Added to Electronic Warfare rolls and to air-to-air missile attacks. Leave blank for no radar.
Aircraft.gunsightOnlyHint: A radar gunsight only: it does not count for Electronic Warfare or missile attacks.
Aircraft.epmHint: Electronic Protection Measures 0–4: a Defence bonus against missiles (chaff, flares, jammers).
Aircraft.superHint: Super rating 0–4: added to Performance only when disengaging or chasing a disengaging enemy, never in a dogfight.
Aircraft.bvrHint: Beyond-visual-range capable: has the radar and missiles for a BVR engagement. Also granted by a BVR trait.
Aircraft.threatHint: Couriers and bombers with turrets: enemies roll Strafing against this number instead of Dogfighting. 0 = none.
Aircraft.usingCrew: using the crew block (no pilot linked)
Aircraft.crippledWarning: Crippled: automatically loses Dogfighting rolls, −3 to everything, difficulty 6 Piloting roll to land.
Aircraft.superHintShort: Super {super}: add it to Performance when disengaging or chasing a disengaging plane.
Aircraft.noStunts: Stunts need Performance 3 or more and an aircraft that is not Trailing Smoke or Crippled.
Aircraft.epmHintShort: EPM {epm} is added to Defence against missiles.
Aircraft.crewIgnored: {name} is flying this aircraft, so the crew block below is ignored.
Aircraft.crewHint: No pilot actor is linked, so the ratings on the Cockpit tab use these numbers. Fill them in for enemy fighters and NPC wingmen.
Aircraft.hardpointsOver: More ordinance mounted than the airframe has hard points. Check the pylons on each weapon.
Aircraft.bailOutHintCrippled: Crippled: posts the rule (limp to safety and bail out rather than risk a crash landing). No roll is needed yet.
Aircraft.bailOutHintDown: Going Down: posts the rule (the pilot bails out at the last second; trapped if Life is on the Line). Turn on the gritty rules in the system settings for the 1d6 + Spirit vs 5 roll.
Aircraft.bailOutHintRoll: Going Down under the gritty rules: rolls the pilot's 1d6 + Spirit against 5. Failure means the pilot dies.
Aircraft.grittyOn: Gritty rules (Shoot to Kill) are on: flying always puts Life on the Line, and a pilot Going Down must roll 1d6 + Spirit vs 5 to bail out.
Aircraft.downWarning: Going Down: damage has reached double the Structure. The plane is lost; the pilot bails out or dies with it.
Aircraft.helicopterHint: Helicopter: rolls an extra d6 on Strafing (keep the best), can hover (sitting duck, Shoot Defence, may fire back head-to-head), and bails out on 1d6 + Body + Athletics vs 5.
Aircraft.bailOutHintHelicopter: Helicopter rules: rolls the pilot's 1d6 + Body + Athletics against 5 to jump clear. Failure means riding the wreck down.

Npc.thugHint: Thugs do not roll initiative, have no Health track and are out of the fight on any hit. Every skill roll is 1d6 + the skill bonus.
Npc.oneHit: No Health track: any hit knocks a thug out of the fight.
Npc.weaponsPlaceholder: Lead +2 damage for pistol (6 shots), Lead +1 for knife
Npc.thugSkillsHint: Only skills with a level are shown for thugs.
Npc.overrideHint: Tick to use the typed stat-block value instead of the number computed from stats and skills.

Table.knackTooltip: Knack: roll 2d6 and keep either die.
Table.name: Name
Table.skillsHint: 1d6 + stat + level; Knack rolls 2d6 and keeps one.

UI.noWeaponsMounted: Nothing mounted. Drag weapons here or add them on the Loadout tab.
UI.rearmHint: Rearm: refill every ammo counter and recharge capacitor weapons (between scenes)

Gear.hint: Equipped armour adds to Resist and shields add to Defence. A flight jacket is +1 Resist and free for pilots.
Gear.valueHint: Value is compared against Fame/Rank when buying: lower buys freely, equal needs a Barter roll vs 6 + value, higher cannot be bought.

Weapon.hint: Accuracy is added to the attack roll. Damage is Lead + N. AP ignores that much of the target's Armour. Missiles carry 1 shot per hard point and use the Ordinance skill plus the aircraft's Radar rating.
Weapon.automationHint: Cooldown: rounds to wait after firing (1 = every other round); the loadout shows when the weapon is ready again during a combat. Recharge: capacitor weapons regain 1 shot at the end of each combat round they did not fire, or are refilled with Rearm between scenes. Alternative mode: offered as a checkbox in the attack dialog, with its Accuracy / Lead change.

Trait.situationalHint: The modifiers only apply in some situations (e.g. Frontal Armour when strafing). They are shown but not added to the ratings automatically.
Trait.grantsBvrHint: This trait makes the aircraft BVR capable.
Trait.modifiersHint: Numbers added to the aircraft's stats and ratings while the trait is active (multiplied by times taken).
Trait.grantsHelicopterHint: Rotary-wing rules: an extra d6 on Strafing rolls (keep the best), hovering, and bailing out on 1d6 + Body + Athletics vs 5.
Trait.grantsStrafingDieHint: Rolls an extra d6 on Strafing rolls and keeps the best (stacks with a Knack).

Sponsorship.obligationsPlaceholder: Ad on the plane and jacket, exclusive use of the product, one day off flying to record jingles
Sponsorship.hint: Sponsors pay 1, 2 or 3 FP and drop you on a Scandal (after the first). Contracts pay 1–3 FP; after the first failure, every failed contract costs its FP value.

Item.noDetails: This item type has no details.

Notifications.itemNotAccepted: This sheet does not accept items of type {type}.
Notifications.dropAircraftOnly: Only Aircraft actors can be assigned to a pilot.
Notifications.dropPilotOnly: Only Pilot actors can be assigned to an aircraft.
Notifications.noAircraft: There are no aircraft you own in this world yet.
Notifications.noPilots: There are no pilots you own in this world yet.
Notifications.subsystemDestroyed: {name} is disabled: 1 damage to the main Structure, Threat may drop.
Notifications.damageRedirected: {name} was already disabled: damage went to the main Structure instead.
Notifications.hardpointsOver: {used} hard points in use but the airframe only has {total}.
Notifications.cannotCredit: Only the pilot's owner or the GM can credit this kill.

Roll.modifierHint: Situational bonuses and penalties: Awesome (+1 to +3), help (+1/+2), tactical advantage, darkness, called shots...
Roll.attackModifierHint: Hold bonus (+1/+2), ganging up (+1/+2), tactics, Awesome, called shots (needs Lead 3, -3 damage)...
Roll.knackHint: Rolls two dice; the better die is kept. The other die is shown on the card in case you prefer it.
Roll.unskilled: Unskilled: difficulty +2 (applied as −2 to the roll)
Roll.disengaging: Disengaging or chasing a disengaging plane (Super and disengage traits)
Roll.outnumber1: Outnumber the enemy by one plane
Roll.outnumber2: Outnumber the enemy by two or more planes
Roll.cuttingItClose: Cutting It Close (-1 Strafing and Defence, +1 to attacks)
Roll.noRadar: No radar: this aircraft cannot take part in a BVR engagement.
Roll.useFireButton: Rolled when firing a weapon (the Fire button adds the weapon's Accuracy).
Roll.defenceHint: Pick the defender's choice (Break, Escape, Shoot) or type a number. For a Stunt, enter the defender's rolled Stunt Defence.
Roll.applyEPM: Add the target's EPM {epm} to its Defence (missiles)
Roll.armourHint: The weapon's AP {ap} is subtracted from this before it reduces damage.
Roll.scaleUp: Vehicle attacking a person (damage × 3, -2 to hit)
Roll.noDefenceGiven: No Defence given: compare the totals by hand.
Roll.critFailAvailable: Natural 1 missing by 3+: you may ask the GM for a critical failure (+1 XP, +1 Reserve).
Roll.vesselDefenceHint: Guns pick a part; ordinance hits a random location (spend Reserve to shift the roll). Typed values override the part's numbers.
Roll.customDifficultyHint: Type any target number here (a vessel's Threat, 5 to bail out...). It overrides the list.
Roll.bailOutDown: Going Down: the pilot bails out at the last second. The GM may call for a certain death scenario and require all remaining Reserve to get out in time.
Roll.bailOutTrapped: Going Down with Life on the Line: there is no time to bail out. The pilot dies trapped in the machine.
Roll.bailOutCrippled: Crippled: limp to a safe area and bail out rather than risk a crash landing. Landing takes a difficulty 6 Piloting roll; a failed roll means bailing out at the last second (the GM may call for certain death).
Roll.bailOutCrippledLotl: Crippled with Life on the Line: the pilot is injured as well and passes out after landing or crashing, with the permanent injuries and long healing of being Out of the Fight.
Roll.bailOutGritty: Gritty rules: a pilot whose plane is Going Down rolls 1d6 + Spirit vs 5 to bail out. Failure means the pilot dies.
Roll.bailOutGrittyLater: Gritty rules are on: if the plane ends up Going Down, the pilot must roll 1d6 + Spirit vs 5 to bail out.
Roll.lowLost: Low altitude and lost the last EW roll (carry-over)
Roll.ewResults: Opposed roll: compare Leads. 1–3: the loser reveals their tactic and the winner may change theirs. 3–6: the winner is also +1 to attack and Defence. 7+: the loser is an unaware target (counts as Press, cannot attack, Defence = Performance). A low-altitude winner sneaks into the merge instead.
Roll.bailOutHelicopter: Helicopter: jettison the rotors and jump. 1d6 + Body + Athletics vs 5; failure means riding the wreck to the ground.
Roll.groupedHint: One roll, compared with each target's own Defence (the chosen defence type applies to all; a typed number overrides them).
Roll.secondLocationHint: Heavy bombs hit two different locations; the second never repeats the first.
Roll.coolingDown: Cooling down — ready again on round {round}.
Roll.slowTargetsWarning: {name} has Performance {performance}: this weapon can only hit Performance 0–1 targets.
Roll.antiShipWarning: {name} is not an airship or ship: this weapon can only target those.
Roll.noPersonnelWarning: {name} is a person: this weapon cannot target people.
Roll.firstTargetOnly: Several tokens are targeted; only the first is used.
Roll.fragmentaryHint: Fragmentary: no −2 against person-sized targets, and one roll hits everyone you have targeted in the blast.
Roll.initiativeAutoLose: Crippled: the aircraft automatically loses the Dogfighting roll this round.
Roll.chosenDefence: Chosen on this round's dogfight card: {defence}.

Vessel.threatTooltip: Threat: attackers roll Strafing (1d6 + Performance + Strafing + SA) against this. Failing by N lets up to 3 gunners fire on the way in. Destroyed sub-systems lower it.
Vessel.defenceTooltip: Defence of the main body (usually 3 + Performance; big ships -1 or -2). Sub-systems are usually 2 higher. Adrift ships are Defence 1.
Vessel.structureHint: Filling the track leaves the vessel adrift (Defence 1, Threat 0); double the track destroys it. Penalties apply to its Defence.
Vessel.hitLocationTooltip: Roll d6 for a random ordinance hit
Vessel.locationHint: d6 result(s) that hit this unit, e.g. 4 or 4 5
Vessel.attackEnabled: This unit can shoot (gun emplacement, battery, turret)
Vessel.specialPlaceholder: Special: destroying the bridge gives -2 Defence; engines out -> Performance 0...
Vessel.reductionHint: Every N destroyed units of this group lower Threat (and damage the main Structure) by the amount. Most: 1 x -1; escort frigate emplacements: 3 x -1.
Vessel.noSubsystems: No sub-systems. Each entry is one unit: add four entries for four gun emplacements.
Vessel.reserveShift: Spend Reserve to shift the location roll up or down.
Vessel.rulesHint: Disabling a unit does 1 damage to the main Structure. Hitting an already disabled unit damages the main Structure instead. Strafers who beat the Threat take one retaliatory shot (Break Defence) on the way out.

outcomeHint.headToHead: No Dogfighting roll: both fighters fire at once with Gunnery or Ordinance and both use Shoot Defence.
outcomeHint.dogfight: The fighters merge: roll Dogfighting as normal (High altitude gives +1 on the first round).
outcomeHint.bvr: Missiles fly at range and the fighters stay beyond visual range. Each may shift one altitude block before the next Electronic Warfare roll.
outcomeHint.disengage: Both fighters drag away from each other: the engagement is over.

Bvr.resolveHint: Compare both fighters' secret tactics once the Electronic Warfare roll is settled (Jet Age p8).
Bvr.secretCard: Secret choice: only you and the GM can see this.

Dogfight.title: Dogfight
Dogfight.outnumber: {side} flight outnumbers the other {own} to {other}: +{bonus} to its Dogfighting rolls.
Dogfight.waiting: Waiting for every aircraft's Dogfighting roll…
Dogfight.oneSided: No opposing aircraft in the fight: nobody has anyone to shoot.
Dogfight.standoff: {a} and {b} tied with equal SA: neither may shoot the other.
Dogfight.manual: Holds, disengage attempts and head-to-heads are resolved by hand. A defence choice applies to every attack on that aircraft this round and the Fire dialog defaults to it.

choice.break: Break Defence against every attack this round.
choice.escape: Escape Defence: the aircraft must disengage next round.
choice.shoot: Shoot Defence (−2): fires back after being shot at.
choice.stunt: Stunt Defence: the rolled value is used against every attack this round.

EnemyFlight.title: Create enemy flight
EnemyFlight.prefixHint: The copies are named prefix + number (Red 1, Red 2…) and placed in the 'Enemy Flights' folder, each with its own linked actor.
EnemyFlight.gradeHint: Picking a grade fills in the numbers below; change them freely. Regular, Squadron Leader and Strafing Ace follow the core book's NPC examples (p162, p166); Rookie and Ace are table defaults.
EnemyFlight.saveGrade: Save these numbers as the default for this grade
EnemyFlight.gmOnly: Only the GM can create enemy flights.
EnemyFlight.noAircraft: There are no aircraft in this world to copy; import one from a compendium first.

TestFight.title: Test Fight
TestFight.gmOnly: Only the GM can set up a test fight.
TestFight.replace: A test fight already exists. Delete it (its actors, scene and combat) and build a new one?
TestFight.created: Created {friendlies} against {enemies}, with tokens on the Test Fight scene and a combat ready.
TestFight.next: Click Begin Combat in the combat tracker: everyone rolls Dogfighting, the round card appears, and the losers pick their defence. Target an enemy token and Fire from a cockpit to shoot.
